# Falcata Run

> Falcata Run is a sprint training app for iPhone and Apple Watch, built for sprinters in any sport that trains explosive speed — track and field, football (40-yard dash), rugby, soccer, field hockey, and more. With an Apple Watch it captures motion data at 100 Hz and delivers sprint-specific metrics — reaction time, drive force, cadence, stride length, arm drive efficiency, and time to max speed — that generic running apps cannot measure. The Apple Watch is optional: the iPhone app is a complete standalone training log with live manual workouts (log sprints between reps, Training Timer, pause/resume, HealthKit heart rate) and after-the-fact session logging (sets × reps, times, recoveries, timing-method provenance: hand timer / electronic / video / Falcata Watch). Manual and Watch reps share one dashboard, trends, and fastest-times list; manual entries never enter sensor-based biomechanics, leaderboards, or validation pipelines. Tagline: "The gold standard for sprint tracking." Website: https://falcatarun.com

> Built by Radim Šimánek (https://github.com/Rad1m, https://www.linkedin.com/in/radim-simanek/). Sister app to Ahimo (https://ahimo.app), a privacy-first iOS health app. Personal blog: https://brainintheloop.com.

## Falcata Analyzer (macOS)

Falcata Analyzer is a native macOS app (macOS 15+) that opens sprint sessions exported from the iPhone and reuses the same engine as the Watch and iPhone (single source of truth — no separate desktop calculation path). It provides synchronized velocity / drive force / power / acceleration / arm-swing / ground-contact charts on one shared playhead, pop-out chart windows, a video editing workspace (link external footage, align to acceleration onset, trim, frame-accurate scrub, edit Start/Finish/Distance markers), a configurable telemetry video overlay, and export to video (H.264 MP4/QuickTime with resolution/FPS/bitrate control), chart images (PNG/JPEG), and CSV. It also supports standalone video analysis (open any video with no linked sprint and mark Start/Finish/Distance markers to measure velocity and acceleration, the same marker-based method as the web analyzer) and on-device AI Vision pose analysis on any marked video segment: a frame-by-frame skeleton overlay with optional lean vectors, video-derived cadence and ground contact time, torso lean, knee drive, touchdown reach, and a per-step metrics table — no sensor data required, results persist per video, and the skeleton can bake into exported clips (landscape or vertical 9:16 portrait). A Team workspace organizes athletes into squads (coach mode: squad-sectioned roster; athlete mode: a personal "My Progress" dashboard) with per-athlete progression dashboards, and a guided analysis wizard walks non-editors from video import to results step by step. Per-sprint units let one sprint display in meters and another in yards (40-yard dash) simultaneously. It replaced the earlier Python desktop video/analysis tooling. Falcata Analyzer also includes an optional AI Sprint Coach with three provider tiers — on-device Apple Intelligence, on-device local MLX/Hugging Face open models, or bring-your-own-key cloud APIs (Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter) — including a chat that retrieves facts across the whole imported sprint history. On-device providers keep all data on the Mac; any cloud use is gated behind an explicit risk consent. (AI coaching is a macOS-Analyzer feature; the iPhone and Watch apps do not require or include it.)

## Falcata Web Analyzer (web)

Falcata Web Analyzer (https://app.falcatarun.com) is a free, install-free, browser-only companion that brings Falcata's marker-based video analysis to any sprint clip — no Apple Watch, no account, no upload. The user opens a local video, scrubs it frame by frame, and places distance markers (Start / Distance / Finish, with a single Start at 0 m and a single Finish) and ground contact time (GCT) contact→toe-off spans. From those markers it derives per-segment velocity, launch acceleration, and a sprint summary (duration, max average speed, start acceleration), validates markers against the Start–Finish window (out-of-bounds flagging), draws a WYSIWYG overlay, and exports a PNG, a short sprint-window video clip (WebM/MP4 with source audio), or a CSV (SI columns). Display units switch between metric and imperial. Markers, playhead, and units auto-save per video file in the browser (IndexedDB); video bytes are never stored or uploaded. It also includes AI Vision: on-device pose analysis on a marked section that traces a frame-by-frame skeleton, detects foot strikes and measures ground contact automatically (read-only AI GCT bars), counts contacts split left/right, and flags overstriding (foot landing ahead of the body, possible/likely severity). AI Vision runs entirely in the browser with no upload, persists results per video file, and in V1 analyzes one section at a time (sections over 30 seconds are blocked). This is on-device computer-vision pose analysis, distinct from the LLM-based AI Sprint Coach, which is a macOS-Analyzer-only feature. (Falcata Analyzer on macOS has its own, richer AI Vision pose analysis — see above.) Unlike the Watch/iPhone/Mac apps it does not use 100 Hz sensor telemetry — it is the manual, hardware-free, video-only side of Falcata, complementary to Falcata Analyzer on macOS (which overlays measured Watch telemetry on footage). Built with React + Vite, hosted on Netlify; analytics are strictly opt-in behind a cookie-consent banner.

## Key facts

- App name: Falcata Run (also referred to as Falcata Sprint Run)
- Platforms: iPhone (standalone training log + analyst companion), Apple Watch (optional 100 Hz capture device), Mac (Falcata Analyzer, macOS 15+ desktop review/video/export app), Web (Falcata Web Analyzer, browser-only marker-based video tool at app.falcatarun.com)
- Apple Watch is optional: iPhone supports live manual workouts and after-the-fact session logging; sensor metrics (reaction time, drive force, etc.) require the Watch
- Target distances: 100m, 200m, 400m, 800m, plus imperial distances (e.g. 40-yard dash) via per-sprint units in Falcata Analyzer, plus free runs
- Audience: sprinters in any sport (track and field, football, rugby, soccer, field hockey), sprint coaches, teams, masters athletes
- Sample rate: 100 Hz accelerometer, gyroscope, and gravity
- Reaction time accuracy: ±10 milliseconds
- Sprint end detection: 3-phase piecewise linear fit (validated 20m–800m)
- Distance source: Apple sensor-fused track-aware distance samples (not raw GPS polyline)
- Key algorithms: velocity-differentiation propulsive G-force, gyroscope peak/bottom step detection, curve compensation with centripetal removal and wrist-aware asymmetry scaling
- Website: https://falcatarun.com
